task.name: A decision notification omits the run identifier and the permitted actions, so the operator it is sent to cannot answer without reaching the machine
task.story_text:
## Why

When a run needs an operator decision it writes a pending record, sends a notification, and waits.
The record holds everything needed to answer: the run id the decision is keyed to, the phase, the
reason, and the exact set of actions permitted. The notification carries none of that.

What goes out is a title naming the story and a body summarising the situation — cycle count, spend,
duration, the last blocking finding, the branch. There is no run id, so the recipient cannot address
the decision, and no option list, so they cannot know what may be chosen. The command that records an
answer takes exactly those two things: a run id and an action.

The result is that a notification which exists to reach an operator who is away cannot be acted on
from away. It reports that something needs deciding and withholds both of the values required to
decide it, so the recipient has to reach the machine and re-derive from the pending file what the
message already knew. On a run where nobody reached the machine in time, the gate expired, and the
wait bought nothing it was configured to buy.

This is the difference between a longer wait and a usable one. Extending the wait only helps if it
can be answered during the extension.

## Example

What is written to the pending record, and what the notification for that same gate carries:

```
pending record                          notification
──────────────────────────────────      ─────────────────────────────
run_id:  65273305e89c                   (absent)
options: accept                         (absent)
         land_core_defer_edges
         redirect
         decompose
         elevate
         defer_or_abandon
phase:   ESCALATE                       (absent)
reason:  quorum unmet, 1/2 ...          first 300 chars of reason
story:   issue-2312                     story slug, in the title
```

Answering requires `forge decide <run_id> <action>` — both values the message omits.

A message carrying them is actionable from a phone over a shell session without any inbound
integration:

```
TheForge: decision needed — issue-2312  (ESCALATE)
Quorum unmet: 1/2 succeeded < threshold 2
Reply within 1h 0m:
  forge decide 65273305e89c <accept|land_core_defer_edges|redirect|decompose|elevate|defer_or_abandon>
```

Note that the human-review gate already offers an `extend` action. Surfacing it makes a wait
extendable by the person who is late rather than only by the person at the keyboard.

## Acceptance criteria

- The notification a gate emits for a pending decision carries the identifier that decision is keyed
  to, so a recipient can address it without consulting the machine that sent the message.
- It carries the set of actions the gate will accept an answer against, read from that same source,
  so the choices offered and the choices honoured cannot drift apart.
- It reports the deadline, or the remaining time, so the recipient can tell whether answering is
  still worth doing.
- Where a gate's permitted actions include extending the wait, that action appears among the offered
  choices like any other.
- A decision answered through the documented command path is written against the run it names, and
  the run proceeds as though the answer had been given locally.
- Where a notification cannot carry the full option set, it reports that and names where the complete
  set can be read, rather than sending a truncated list that reads as complete.

## Out of scope

An inbound integration that lets an operator answer by interacting with the message itself. That
needs a receiving endpoint and an auth story, and is worth doing separately once outbound messages
are actionable at all.

handoff.summary: Implemented actionable pending-decision notifications by formatting outbound gate messages from the pending record itself, so the operator receives the exact run id, option set, and deadline the gate will honor. Updated the human-review, escalate, and plan-review pending gates to use that formatter after writing the checkpoint, and added unit/seam tests including the fallback path that omits oversized option lists only when the notification cannot carry them safely.

findings.description: When a pending decision's reason text is longer than the notification budget — the normal case for an ESCALATE gate, whose reason is a rendered advisory report — the emitted body drops the permitted-action list and sends the generic 'forge decide <run-id> <action>' plus a read-the-file notice, even though the six-action taxonomy is under a hundred characters and would fit once the reason is trimmed; the emitted body is also 902 characters against a declared 900-character budget.

finding_registry.description: When a pending decision's reason text is longer than the notification budget — the normal case for an ESCALATE gate, whose reason is a rendered advisory report — the emitted body drops the permitted-action list and sends the generic 'forge decide <run-id> <action>' plus a read-the-file notice, even though the six-action taxonomy is under a hundred characters and would fit once the reason is trimmed; the emitted body is also 902 characters against a declared 900-character budget.

When every fallback layout still exceeds the character budget, the final branch hard-truncates the composed body, so the message can end in a partially written command such as 'forge deci...' or a clipped run identifier that reads like a complete instruction but cannot be pasted.

When every candidate layout exceeds the character budget — for example a budget smaller than the run identifier itself, or a record with no run identifier under a small budget — the formatter returns an empty string, so the gate sends a notification with no body at all.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
